# Plan: typed CRUD mount functions generated by `ormc`

Context: master `webtyp/docs/ARCHITECTURE_MASTER_PLAN.md` D12, D13. Without generics, a module writes
`list.(*PatientList)` by hand; pairing `&FloorList{}` with `(*RoomList)` compiles and panics on the first request.
`ormc` already knows each entity and its `<Name>List`, so it generates the typed wrappers and the module never writes
a type assertion for records (a read filter is still `model.Model`, asserted by the module).

This repo is backend tooling: stdlib (`os`, `strings`, `path/filepath`) is legitimate here — do NOT "fix" it.

## Tools

```bash
go install webtyp.com/devflow/cmd/gotest@latest
```

## What is generated (exact output for an entity `Patient`, `ModelName` `patient`, in `model.go`)

File `model_crud.go` (`<source without .go>_crud.go`, next to `model_orm.go`), **no build tag** (demos mount modules in the browser through `crud.Loopback`):

```go
// DO NOT EDIT. generated by webtyp.com/ormc

package patientdirectory

import (
	"webtyp.com/crud"
	"webtyp.com/model"
)

// MountPatientCreate mounts the create operation of Patient with a typed batch.
func MountPatientCreate(reg crud.Registry, create func(c crud.Caller, list PatientList) error) crud.Route {
	return reg.Create(func() model.ModelSlice { return &PatientList{} }, func(c crud.Caller, l model.ModelSlice) error {
		return create(c, *l.(*PatientList))
	})
}

// MountPatientRead mounts the read operation of Patient; newFilter may be nil (no filter).
func MountPatientRead(reg crud.Registry, newFilter func() model.Model, read func(c crud.Caller, args crud.ReadArgs, filter model.Model) (PatientList, error)) crud.Route {
	return reg.Read(&Patient{}, newFilter, func(c crud.Caller, args crud.ReadArgs, filter model.Model) (model.ModelSlice, error) {
		list, err := read(c, args, filter)
		return &list, err
	})
}

// MountPatientUpdate mounts the update operation of Patient with a typed carrier record.
func MountPatientUpdate(reg crud.Registry, update func(c crud.Caller, ids, fields []string, rec Patient) error) crud.Route {
	return reg.Update(func() model.Model { return &Patient{} }, func(c crud.Caller, ids, fields []string, rec model.Model) error {
		return update(c, ids, fields, *rec.(*Patient))
	})
}

// MountPatientDelete mounts the delete operation of Patient.
func MountPatientDelete(reg crud.Registry, remove func(c crud.Caller, ids []string) error) crud.Route {
	return reg.Delete(&Patient{}, remove)
}
```

## Rules

1. Generated only when the nearest `go.mod` above the source file (walk up from `filepath.Dir(sourceFile)`) has a
   `require` of `webtyp.com/crud` (a line whose first field, after trimming and an optional leading `require`, is
   `webtyp.com/crud`). Otherwise no `_crud.go` is written and an existing one is deleted (`os.Remove`, ignore
   `os.IsNotExist`). A package without crud must still compile.
2. Only for entities with a table: `!info.NoDB && !info.Wire && !info.IsForm`. If none qualifies, write no file (delete a stale one).
3. Entity order = the order of `infos` (same as `model_orm.go`).
4. The four functions always appear; the Go linker drops the unused ones.
5. `packageDefinitions` (`generate.go:468`) also skips `_crud.go`.

## Stage 1 — `crud_gen.go` (new)

```go
// requiresCrud reports whether the go.mod that owns dir requires webtyp.com/crud.
func requiresCrud(dir string) (bool, error)

// writeCrudFile writes (or removes) <source>_crud.go for the table entities of infos.
func (o *Generator) writeCrudFile(infos []StructInfo, sourceFile string) error
```
Constants: `crudImport = "webtyp.com/crud"`, `crudFileSuffix = "_crud.go"`. Build the text with `fmt.Convert()` like `GenerateForFile`;
run `go/format.Source` on it before writing. Call `o.writeCrudFile(infos, sourceFile)` at the end of `GenerateForFile`, after
`model_orm.go` is written (`generate.go:440`: write the orm file, then return `o.writeCrudFile(...)`).
